ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and 0 <= j <= floor(r (b - a) / 2). Put I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|, and assume M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Let X_j be the set of pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, |lambda| denotes the sum of the elements of lambda, and |lambda| + sum_{s in S} (r + s) = j. Then there exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that: (1) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S',lambda') != (S,lambda), then |S'| is congruent to |S| + 1 modulo 2; and (2) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S,lambda), then |S| is even.

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.proof_nl:
Let J_t := (f_s : a+1 <= s <= t) for t = a, a+1, ..., b, with J_a := (0), and let B_t := R/J_t. Then B_a = R and B_b = A. Since every f_s is homogeneous, each J_t is a homogeneous ideal, so each B_t is a graded Q-algebra. Also each degree piece (B_t)_n is finite-dimensional over Q because it is a quotient of R_n.

First compute the Hilbert series of R. The monomials product_{s=a+1}^b x_s^{e_s}, with e_s in Z_{>=0}, form a Q-basis of R, and such a monomial has degree sum_{s=a+1}^b s e_s. Hence R_n has basis indexed by tuples (e_s) with sum s e_s = n; there are only finitely many such tuples because all s are positive. Therefore
Hilb_R(q) = sum_{(e_s)} q^(sum s e_s)
= product_{s=a+1}^b (sum_{m >= 0} q^(m s))
= product_{s=a+1}^b 1/(1 - q^s).

Now fix t with a+1 <= t <= b, and put d_t := r + t. Since t >= a+1 >= 1 and r >= 0, we have d_t > 0. Because the ordered list (f_{a+1}, f_{a+2}, ..., f_b) is a regular sequence, the class of f_t in B_{t-1} is a non-zero-divisor. Moreover B_t = B_{t-1}/(f_t), where (f_t) now denotes the ideal of B_{t-1} generated by the class of f_t. Since f_t is homogeneous of degree d_t, for each n >= 0 the degree-n part of that ideal is exactly f_t (B_{t-1})_{n-d_t}, with the convention (B_{t-1})_m = 0 for m < 0. Thus for each n >= 0 we have an exact sequence of Q-vector spaces
0 -> (B_{t-1})_{n-d_t} -- multiplication by f_t -> (B_{t-1})_n -> (B_t)_n -> 0.
Therefore
dim_Q (B_t)_n = dim_Q (B_{t-1})_n - dim_Q (B_{t-1})_{n-d_t}.
Summing over n >= 0 gives
Hilb_{B_t}(q) = (1 - q^(d_t)) Hilb_{B_{t-1}}(q).

Iterating this identity from t = a+1 up to t = b, and using the formula for Hilb_R(q), we obtain
Hilb_A(q) = Hilb_{B_b}(q)
= (product_{s=a+1}^b (1 - q^(r+s))) Hilb_R(q)
= product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s))/(1 - q^s)).

By the definition of Hilbert series, this means that for every j >= 0, the coefficient of q^j in product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s))/(1 - q^s)) is exactly dim_Q A_j. In particular, every such coefficient is a nonnegative integer.

It remains to prove that A is finite-dimensional. For any real u with 0 < u < 1, the series sum_{n >= 0} (dim_Q A_n) u^n converges because dim_Q A_n <= dim_Q R_n and
sum_{n >= 0} (dim_Q R_n) u^n = product_{s=a+1}^b 1/(1 - u^s) < infinity.
So we may evaluate the identity above at such a real u:
sum_{n >= 0} (dim_Q A_n) u^n = product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - u^(r+s))/(1 - u^s)).

For each fixed s,
(1 - u^m)/(1 - u) = 1 + u + ... + u^(m-1),
so
lim_{u -> 1^-} (1 - u^(r+s))/(1 - u^s) = (r+s)/s.
Hence the right-hand side has a finite limit product_{s=a+1}^b ((r+s)/s) as u -> 1^-; in particular it stays bounded near u = 1.

Suppose, for contradiction, that A_n != 0 for infinitely many n. Then there are infinitely many n with a_n := dim_Q A_n >= 1. Given any positive integer N, choose distinct indices n_1 < ... < n_N with a_{n_i} >= 1. For u sufficiently close to 1, we have u^{n_i} > 1/2 for all i, and then
sum_{n >= 0} a_n u^n >= sum_{i=1}^N u^{n_i} > N/2.
Since N is arbitrary, the left-hand side would be unbounded as u -> 1^-, contradicting the boundedness of the right-hand side. Therefore A_n = 0 for all but finitely many n. As each A_n is finite-dimensional, A = direct sum_{n >= 0} A_n is finite-dimensional over Q.

Thus A is a finite-dimensional graded Q-algebra, its Hilbert series is exactly product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s))/(1 - q^s)), and the coefficient of q^j in that product is dim_Q A_j and hence a nonnegative integer for every j >= 0.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Given integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, and given a finite indexed family of homogeneous polynomials f_s in the weighted graded polynomial ring R = Q[x_s : s in I] with I = {a+1, ..., b}, deg(x_s) = s, deg(f_s) = r+s, and with the f_s forming a regular sequence in increasing index order, the quotient algebra A = R divided by the ideal generated by the f_s is finite-dimensional over Q. Its Hilbert series is exactly the product over s from a+1 to b of (1 minus q to the power r+s) divided by (1 minus q to the power s). Consequently, for every nonnegative integer j, the coefficient of q to the j in that product equals dim_Q of A_j and is a nonnegative integer.

Form the graded polynomial ring R over the rational numbers with variables x_s for s in I, where x_s has degree s.
For every s in I, choose a homogeneous polynomial f_s in R of degree r+s.
Require that the family (f_s) ordered by increasing s is a regular sequence.
Define A as the quotient of R by the ideal generated by all f_s.
For every nonnegative integer n, let A_n be the degree-n component of A.
Conclude that A is finite-dimensional over Q and that its Hilbert series equals the stated product.
For every nonnegative integer j, the coefficient of degree j in the product equals dim_Q A_j and is a nonnegative integer.

payload.statement_nl:
Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}, let R := Q[x_s : s in I] be graded by deg(x_s) = s, and let (f_s)_{s in I} be a family of homogeneous polynomials in R such that deg(f_s) = r+s for every s in I and the ordered list by increasing s is a regular sequence. Put A := R / (f_s : s in I), and let A_n denote the degree-n homogeneous component of A. Then A is a finite-dimensional graded Q-algebra and its Hilbert series is
Hilb_A(q) = sum_{n >= 0} (dim_Q A_n) q^n = product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)).
In particular, for every integer j >= 0, the coefficient [q^j] product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) equals dim_Q A_j and is a nonnegative integer.

dependency_assessment.notes: Proof uses only standard consequences of the given regular-sequence hypothesis and graded Hilbert series computations; no external cited lemma was invoked.

detailed_findings.finding: The exact sequence on degree-n pieces is correctly justified from homogeneity of f_t and the non-zero-divisor property in B_{t-1}.
The proof of finite-dimensionality is indirect but valid: boundedness of the evaluated Hilbert series near u = 1 rules out infinitely many nonzero graded pieces.

result_payload.reason: The proof matches the stated lemma and is mathematically complete. It correctly computes the Hilbert series of the weighted polynomial ring R, then uses the regular-sequence hypothesis to obtain for each t the short exact sequence on graded pieces induced by multiplication by the homogeneous non-zero-divisor f_t, yielding Hilb_{B_t}(q) = (1 - q^{r+t}) Hilb_{B_{t-1}}(q). Iteration gives the claimed product formula for Hilb_A. The identification of coefficients with dim_Q A_j is immediate from the Hilbert series definition, giving nonnegativity. The remaining finite-dimensionality claim is also proved: for 0 < u < 1 the generating series converges and equals the finite product, whose limit as u -> 1^- is finite; if infinitely many A_n were nonzero, the series would become unbounded near 1, contradiction. No substantial omissions or illegal dependencies were detected.
